notes: Single quiet, day-grouped agenda column maintained at all three widths — no dashboard grid, no competing panels; at 900px the agenda column visibly caps well short of the viewport with empty margin either side, matching DESIGN.md's max-640px rule.
No horizontal overflow or edge-clipped rows spotted at 375px or 393px across the captured agenda (today through roughly 8. november) — the narrowest width, most prone to breaking, held up.

Match names render as complete two-sided fixtures with no visible truncation/ellipsis in the rows that were legible — e.g. 'Brann – Molde', '1. FC Union Berlin – Cologne', 'Liverpool – Arsenal', 'Eintracht Frankfurt – Hamburg SV', 'Bayern München – Borussia Dortmund' — including Norwegian club names.

Header (wordmark, date line, search/filter + theme controls), day headings ('I DAG', 'I MORGEN', dated ranges), and the footer/'Dette dekker vi' + install-hint block are all present and aligned at every width.
Team crests/flags render as small filled icons in the rows that were legible, not broken-image placeholders or empty boxes.
Must-see accent dots appear on a minority of rows only, not on every row — consistent with the 'gentlest possible emphasis' rule.

At 393px and 900px the floating 'Assistent' (sparkles) button sits over a mid-agenda row, not the last agenda row or the footer — matches the DESIGN.md-sanctioned floating-button idiom (WP-146 variant D); correctly not flagged as a bug. At 900px it also sits clear of the capped-width column's empty margin in places, which is likewise sanctioned.

Limitation: the 375px and 393px full-page captures are very tall (~22-24k px at deviceScaleFactor 2) and were viewed as single downscaled images, so fine per-character legibility (confirming every individual channel label, or scrutinizing every crest) could not be verified with full confidence beyond the layout-level checks above. Within what was legible, no channel resembling a foreign broadcaster (FOX/ESPN/Sky) was spotted, and no row appeared to be missing a channel/'–' slot or a round label where one would be expected.
